newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Wafangdian B shares up 9.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Wafangdian B shares up 9.2 pct.

text.p: Wafangdian Bearing Co's foreign currency B shares jumped HK$0.59 or 9.2 percent to HK$7.0 in mid-morning on the Shenzhen stock exchange on Monday on investors' belief the price was still low despite strong recent gains, brokers said.
It was also the most actively traded stock on volume of 4.06 million shares by 11.00 a.m. (0300 GMT).
"The P/E (price/earnings ratio) is low compared with other B shares and investors tend to favour new shares," an analyst at J&A Securities in Shenzhen said.

Wafangdian, the only company to be listed on the Shenzhen B share market so far this year, posted per-share earnings of 0.5 yuan for the January-September period of 1996 against 0.47 yuan for the whole of 1995, based on Chinese accounting standards.

Wafangdian shares rose strongly last week, partly on reports that its parent company had taken over a high-techology firm, Dalian Instrument Group, even though a spokesman for the company said it would have no direct impact on the listed company.
"Wafangdian keeps rising because as a new share it is less constrained by technical charts," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
Wafangdian, one of China's biggest bearing makers, listed 130 million foreign currency B shares on March 25, of which 65 million were sold to Sweden AB SKF.
